[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/06/15 (Thu) 06:07  
[USER] User is looking for healthy and easy-to-prepare breakfast recipes for busy mornings.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested breakfast recipes include:  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 1. Overnight oats: Mix rolled oats with milk, yogurt, and fruits/toppings, refrigerate overnight.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 2. Yogurt parfait: Layer Greek yogurt with granola and mixed berries.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 3. Smoothie bowl: Blend almond milk, frozen fruits, and spinach/kale; top with chia seeds and sliced fruits.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 4. Avocado toast: Toast whole wheat bread, spread mashed avocado, and sprinkle with salt, pepper, and chili flakes.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 5. Egg muffins: Whisk eggs, cheese, and chopped vegetables; bake in muffin cups for 20 minutes.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 6. Peanut butter banana sandwich: Spread peanut butter on whole grain bread and top with sliced bananas.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 7. Chia seed pudding: Mix chia seeds with almond milk and vanilla extract; refrigerate overnight and top with fruits and nuts.  
[USER] User inquired which breakfast option has the most protein.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] For protein-packed options:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Egg muffins: About 12 grams of protein from two muffins (2 eggs).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Yogurt parfait: Greek yogurt contains around 17 grams of protein per serving.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Smoothie bowl: Greek yogurt can provide up to 23 grams of protein if used.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Peanut butter banana sandwich: Approximately 8 grams of protein.  
[USER] User plans to try making the egg muffins tomorrow morning.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Egg muffins are a great choice for a protein-packed breakfast; they are easy to prepare and customizable.  
[USER] User asked if they can make the egg muffins ahead of time and reheat them in the morning.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Yes, egg muffins can be made ahead and stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4 days.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To reheat, microwave for 30-60 seconds or freeze for up to 3 months; reheat from frozen for 1-2 minutes in the microwave or bake for 15-20 minutes at 350°F.
